the likelihood of socially responsible behavior by corporations is greater when the following conditions are present: (a) the economic system is characterized by a large number of small, independent firms; (b) the economic system has a high degree of economic development, as measured by the per capita gross domestic product; (c) there is an active and effective public regulatory system that includes the ability of the state to enforce its regulations; (d) there is a well-developed and effective private regulatory system that includes self

the likelihood that a corporation will behave in socially responsible way increases with the following institutional conditions: (a) the presence of public regulation of corporations; (b) the existence of private self-regulation of corporations; (c) the presence of independent organizations that monitor corporations' behavior; (d) the existence of institutionalized norms regarding corporate behavior; (e) associative behavior among corporations; and (f) organized dialogue between corporations and their stakeholders.
the more a society is characterized by a strong civil society and a strong state, the more likely it is that corporations will behave in socially responsible manners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the institutional context and corporate social behavior.
the conditions under which corporate social responsibility is likely to occur.
the conditions under which the market mechanism can be expected to produce socially desirable outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the likelihood that a corporation would behave in a socially responsible manner is a function of the following variables: the extent to which the corporation is regulated by the state and other organizations; the extent to which it is monitored by other organizations; the degree to which the corporation has adopted the norms of socially responsible behavior; the degree towhich it is associated with other corporations in socially responsible ways; and the degree to which it is engaged in dialogues with its stakeholders.
the relationship between the basic economic conditions and the behavior of the corporation is mediated by the institutional environment.

the more a society is regulated and the more it has independent organizations, the more it has institutionalized norms, the more it encourages associative behavior, and the more it engages in organized dialogue, the greater will be the extent of corporate social responsibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
corporate social responsibility is an institutionalized phenomenon.
the more the institutional context is supportive, the more likely corporations will behave in a socially responsible manner.
